column1: # V8a LOCUS-DETECTION SPECIFICITY decoy panel (Ludmil, 25 Sep report, section 4 V8a).
# "Challenge pks-supporting reads against pks-negative Enterobacterales, close
#  homologous NRPS/PKS sequences, broad gut/oral backgrounds, GRCh38, and UniVec.
#  This asks whether the sequence really belongs to the pks/clb locus."
# Every member here is meant to be pks/clb NEGATIVE. scripts/build_specificity_panels.py
# screens each downloaded genome against the canonical IHE3034 island and refuses to
# place a member in the decoy panel if its island coverage is at or above
# --max-decoy-island-coverage; a member that fails the screen is written to
# v8a_pks_screen.tsv with status=rejected_pks_positive and left out of the panel, because
# a pks-carrying "decoy" would absorb genuine pks reads and turn a specificity check into
# a coin flip. It is not silently dropped: the screen table is part of the panel.
# GRCh38 and UniVec are not accessions here. GRCh38 is passed as a local FASTA
# (--grch38), because the copy that matters is the one the cohort was aligned against and
# it is already on disk; UniVec is fetched from NCBI by --univec. Both are recorded in
# v8a_panel_members.tsv exactly like the accession-driven members.

column4: Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655
column5: Reference E. coli, phylogroup A, no pks island: the nearest whole-genome neighbour of IHE3034 that must not absorb clb reads.
Phylogroup E EHEC; large accessory genome and many prophages, pks-negative.
E. coli by ANI; the strictest same-species-level decoy after K-12.

column4: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium str. LT2
column5: Enterobacterales outside Escherichia; common gut/clinical background.
Citrobacter genus control against the pks+ C. koseri in the V8b carrier panel: genus alone must not confirm the locus.
Enterobacter genus control against the pks+ Enterobacter/K. aerogenes candidates in V8b.
Morganellaceae; NRPS-bearing Enterobacterales further from E. coli.
Yersiniaceae; carries its own NRPS/PKS secondary metabolism (prodigiosin).
Carries the yersiniabactin HMWP1/HMWP2 NRPS-PKS megasynthases, the classic domain-level look-alike of clbB/clbC/clbJ/clbK.
pksX/bacillaene: the textbook trans-AT PKS, the same architecture clbB-clbO uses. A read that is really a megasynthase-domain read should be competitive here.
Multiple trans-AT PKS/NRPS clusters (pyoluteorin, orfamide, pederin-like) in one genome.
Enterobacterales with an exceptionally NRPS/PKS-rich genome: homologous domains on a closely related genomic background.
More than twenty PKS/NRPS clusters; the densest single-genome source of ketosynthase and adenylation domains.
Pyoverdine/pyochelin NRPS; common clinical and sequencing background.
Abundant gut anaerobe; carried over from the phase-1 panel.
Type-strain gut Bacteroides, distinct from B. fragilis.
Most abundant gut Firmicute; carried over from the phase-1 panel.
Mucin-degrading Verrucomicrobia; carried over from the phase-1 panel.
Actinobacterial gut background, high GC.
Gut/clinical Firmicute frequently co-detected with CRC samples.
Low-GC Clostridia, a very different composition from the island.
Gut Lachnospiraceae; makes its own NRPS-derived metabolite.
Dominant butyrate producer in colonic samples.
Enterotype-defining gut Bacteroidetes.
Oral/gut organism with its own CRC association: the most biologically loaded decoy for this cohort.
Oral pathogen; carried over from the phase-1 panel.
Oral Streptococcus; carried over from the phase-1 panel.
Mitis-group Streptococcus, the commonest oral contaminant genus in tumour sequencing.
Oral/gut Negativicutes.
Oral Bacteroidetes.
Oral anaerobe repeatedly reported in CRC tumour tissue.
Oral Pasteurellaceae (Gammaproteobacteria), between the oral and Enterobacterales arms.
The other classic CRC-associated organism; must not be mistaken for a pks carrier.
